Bc.bar_b_note: A grounded, correctly scaled moss toad, but its single mid-green value with no separated belly, eye or rim light, and a faint-end pose that reads as a moss lump, sit below Palworld's crisp creature read.

Sm.bar_b_note: Side B's lime-and-black camouflage swallows the face and silhouette in every pose, and side A is the same muddy single-value moss toad as Bc.

Fy.bar_b_note: Smeared low-resolution ground, flat sky, untextured tunnel walls and a uniform tree wall sink it, although side B's aftermaths (freed villager, toppled banners, smoking out fire) tell a clear story.

Sb.bar_b_note: Close to the owner bar for naturalistic fur and mass, but the back plates read as a regular grid of cube tiles, the faint end goes near-black, and side B's red glow and reddish tusks drift toward the reserved danger red.

Ud.bar_b_note: A murky brown grade with no purple storm sky or lightning, flat magenta telegraph rings and wedges, a heavy HUD, and (on side A) foliage filling the camera leave this far from a Palworld boss fight.

Tj.bar_b_note: A clean, appealing elder villager with readable eyes and an earthy green-brown outfit that fits the key art, held back only by a slightly more cartoon face than the naturalistic creatures and a stiff full-body pose.

top_changes.change: Stormwood fights (Ud): replace the flat magenta telegraph rings and wedges with grounded effects (cracking ground, white-violet lightning arcs, debris on impact), fade or collide the camera through trunks and canopy, push a purple storm sky with blue-green moss grade, and slim the left HUD panel.

Meadows ground and aftermath (Fy): swap the smeared ground material for a crisp grass and earth blend with clumped grass and flower cards, texture the tunnel walls, and in every after frame take down or topple the enemy banner and leave a site-specific trace (the side B approach).

Creature materials (Bc, Sm, Sb): split values so the face reads (pale belly and throat, golden eye with catch-light and rim light on the moss toad), drop the camouflage pattern, keep emissive and tusk colours off dark red, and break up the boar's grid of cube back plates with irregular stones.
